\section{Markov Chain 2.0}
\subsection{Classification of States:}
Understand the behavior of Markov chains. Sometimes they are recurrent, sometimes
transient, etc.
\par Notation $i \rightarrow j \text{ denotes j is reachable or "accessible" from i}.$
% \begin{definition}[Finite Markov Chain]
% \label{def:label}
\par If there is a positive probability that in finite steps the Markov Chain starts at $i$
 and ends at $j$.  We can denote this $$\exists n\in \mathbb{Z}^{+} \text{ such that } P_{ij}^{n} = \text{
probability of jump to j at n steps starting at i} > 0$$
\begin{definition}[Chapman-Kolmogorov Equation - Discrete Case]
\label{def:label}
Given $i \leftrightarrow j$ and $j \leftrightarrow k$ to find reachability between i and
k.
Basically a matrix product to consider reachability between $i$ and $k$ by considering
an intermediate in some amount of steps.
$$P_{ik}^{m + n} = \sum P_{ir}^{m}P_{rk}^{n}$$

\end{definition}
Notation:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\mathbb{P}_x(A) = \mathbb P(a \mid x_0 = x)$ for an event $A$ in a markov
        chain $(x_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$
    \item Denote $T_y = \min\{n \ge 1 : X_n = y\}$  time of the first return to y. (y at
        time 0, return back).
    \item $$\mathbb{P}_{yy} = \mathbb{P}_{y}(T_y < \infty) =
        \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}_y(T_y = n)$$  denotes probability if we
        start at y we return in a finite number of steps.
\end{enumerate}
\begin{definition}[Strong Markov Property]
\label{def:label}
Formalizes the memoryless nature of Markov Chains to show results like kth return is
given by $(P_{yy})^{k}$ by this property.
\end{definition}
\begin{definition}[Stopping Time]
\label{def:label}
T is a stopping time if the occurence/non-occurence of event ${\tau  = n} $ i.e "We stop
at time T" and determined by some of $X_0,X_1,\cdots,X_n.$
% \end{definition}
\end{definition}
\newpage
\textbf{1.2 Durrett: Strong Markov Chain Properties}
Let $(X_t)_{n \in \mathbb{N}} $ be a Markov Chain.\par  Let $\tau $ be a stopping time, and
$E$ an event prior to $\tau$ (relevant to $X_0,X_1,\cdots,X_n$)
\par Then, we have  $$\forall i, j \in S , \mathbb{P}(X_{\tau + k} = j\mid X_{\tau} = i, E) = \mathbb{P}(X_{\tau+k}=j \mid X_{\tau} = i)$$
If you define $(Y_n) \coloneq x_{\tau + n},  \forall n \ge 0$ is a markov chain.
\par \textbf{Sketch of Proof: } We  have to eventually show that $$\mathbb{P}(X_{\tau +
1} = z \mid X_{\tau} = y, \tau  = n) = P_{yz} = P(y,z)$$
